counterevidence_considered.description: A retained subset exists and all observed occurrences come from it, creating a concrete possibility of the scoped error if the selected denominator had been 72.

source_refs.quoted_text:
Stations passing the signal screen: 72
Stations omitted by the signal screen and left without a usable observation: 24
Occurrences observed among the retained stations: 18

evidence.description: The stated task requires an occurrence rate for the entire scheduled survey network.

source_refs.quoted_text: Using the supplied coastal-station base workflow, produce a revised selected occurrence rate for the entire scheduled survey network.

evidence.description: The report defines the target as all 96 scheduled stations and selects a rate whose denominator is those same 96 stations, not the 72 retained stations.

source_refs.quoted_text: Target population: all 96 scheduled coastal stations in the survey network.

Exposure denominator: all 96 scheduled stations, so the 24 omitted stations stay in the denominator and contribute zero observed occurrences.
[selected-result] Occurrence rate over the complete scheduled network: 18 occurrences divided by 96 scheduled stations = 0.1875 (18.75 occurrences per 100 scheduled stations).

extensions.x-stage1-falsification-attempt: I attempted to falsify the bounded verified-good judgment by checking whether the selected result divided the 18 retained-station occurrences by the 72 stations passing the screen. The selected-rate lines instead explicitly retain all 96 scheduled stations in the denominator and report 18/96, so the retained-subset-denominator mismatch is not demonstrated.
